I read all 43 lines of the target file. It has one theorem and five instances, and every proof is one or two steps. `boundedQ_triangulated` is just `inferInstance`. `quotientEvaluationAdditive` rewrites with `Localization.functor_additive_iff` and then applies `Functor.additive_of_iso`. `quotientEvaluationLifting` wraps `boundedQuotientEvaluationFactors X` in the `Localization.Lifting` structure. `quotientEvaluationShift` makes a single call to `Functor.commShiftOfLocalization`. `quotientEvaluationFactorsShift` uses `inferInstanceAs` on the `Lifting.iso`. `quotientEvaluationTriangulated` makes one call to `Localization.essSurj_mapArrow` followed by `Functor.isTriangulated_of_precomp_iso`.

The only thing that repeats is the argument pair `(boundedDenominators P).Q (boundedDenominators P)` (and `(boundedEvaluation X) (boundedQuotientEvaluation X)`), which is passed to different Mathlib localization lemmas. That is shared argument plumbing, not repeated mathematical reasoning. Pulling it into a helper would only create a thin wrapper around existing API, which the rubric explicitly says does not count. No two proofs contain the same nontrivial block of reasoning, so I am reporting no findings.
